transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-17 14:30 PST | Duration 48m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jae (Redwood SE), Katrina (Sentinel SecOps), Liam (VP Eng), Priya (DevOps), Tom (CTO)

Auto-generated summary:
- Purpose: Review recent vulnerability findings from 3rd-party scan and internal pen-tests, align on remediation windows and SDLC hardening steps, discuss encryption/KMS and audit log retention for compliance.
- Outcome: Agreed to share artifacts, define triage rubric, run a private-deploy patch window benchmark, and follow up with SOC 2 evidence.

Topics:
- High-level vuln findings and risk exposure
- Patch cadence and canary rollout for Dedicated/Private deployments
- RBAC/SSO (SAML/SCIM) gaps and audit log retention
- Encryption: KMS, CMEK, and key rotation cadence
- SDLC integration: pre-merge scans, ticketing, and release gating

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'r gonna kick off, we've got about forty eight minutes, um so quick intros - maybe Katrina, could you call out the top priorities from your side?
[00:18] Katrina: Yeah thanks Maya. Um the main thing for us is we just finished a third party vuln assessment last week and a couple of issues popped up that touch both hosted and private variants. Most critical ones are CVE-ish rce in a dependency, and some misconfigured audit logging on the private control plane. so we need to know how Redwood handles hot-patch windows, and what audit log retention looks like for Private.
[00:36] Jae: Got it. Can you say if the misconfigured logs are at the infra layer or in the app stack?
[00:44] Katrina: It's mostly infra — the control plane's ELK forwarding had a mis- transform, so a bunch of auth events weren't indexed. also the report flagged SAML assertion time skew problems under heavy load.
[01:00] Liam: To add, we're trying to map out compliance for a customer pilot in EMEA in Q1, so data residency and KMS where keys are region-bound are a hard requirement. This affects whether we use Redwood Hosted or request a Private VPC.
[01:18] Maya: Understood. Let me quickly set expectations: Redwood's Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS (CMEK) and region-bound keys; audit logs can be pushed into your existing SIEM. For hosted we do retain logs for 90 days by default with export options for longer retention on enterprise plans, but we'll need to walk through details.
[01:36] Tom: That 90 days is for token-level traces right? We need immutable audit trails for at least 2 years in the pilot.
[01:44] Maya: Yeah, standard hosted default is shorter — for longer retention we have add-on packages. We'll send the policy doc after.
[01:52] Priya: On patch cadence — our internal policy is weekly patch windows for infra, but we do emergency hotfixes as needed. How does Redwood support canarying model or runtime updates, and can we pin to a model build until our security sign-off?
[02:12] Jae: Yes — you can pin model versions and runtime images. We have canary rollout support with traffic split and automatic rollback thresholds. For urgent CVEs we support a hot-patch path but timeline depends on whether it's a hosted image update or requires infra maintenance in your private VPC.
[02:30] Katrina: And what about the KV cache; earlier scans highlighted stale tokens in KV cash — is that a session persistence issue? (laughs)
[02:38] Jae: (chuckles) yeah KV cache sometimes comes through as "cash" in reports. It's the in-memory KV we use for prefixes — we rotate session tokens per-request and have TTLs, but in Private deployments TTLs are configurable by you.
[02:56] [00:03:10] Liam: Okay, practical ask — we're going to prioritize: 1) RCE in dependency (high), 2) misindexed auth logs (medium), 3) SAML skew (medium). We'll want a mitigation plan and an estimate of time-to-fix.
[03:20] Maya: Great. Jae, can you walk through what a mitigation path looks like for the RCE — is it a model lib or container runtime?
[03:30] Jae: From the quick read — looks like a transitive dependency in a tokenizer lib used in our image. For hosted we can roll a patched image and push within 24-48 hours subject to regression tests; for Private, if you're using Redwood-managed images we can push and coordinate, but if you fork images or run an air-gapped variant it's on you to apply patches, though we provide patched images and a diff.
[03:54] Priya: We're on a mixed model — we use Redwood images but we overlay some init scripts. we'd want to test patched images in a staging private environment before applying to prod.
[04:06] Jae: Absolutely. We can schedule a staging patch window and provide an image tag for you to smoke test.
[04:12] [00:04:30] Katrina: One gaiting question on SDLC — we want pre-merge security scanning to catch these transitive deps before they reach prod. Does Redwood provide any tooling or integrations for SCA in CI?
[04:26] Maya: Redwood doesn't instrument your CI by default, but we provide SBOMs for images and a recommended CI snippet for SCA tools. We'll share an example GitHub Action we use to verify image SBOMs and a policy for blocking merges on critical CVEs.
[04:44] Tom: On RBAC — our internal auditors are asking for fine-grained role mapping: can we map SCIM groups to Redwood console roles and have per-token scoping logs?
[04:56] Jae: Yes, SCIM + SAML SSO is supported, and RBAC roles map to scopes. Token-level auditing is available in Dedicated/Private; hosted offers token traces but for forensic retention you'd go to enterprise logging. There was a note in your report about malformed session tokens — that usually happens when an old key is used before rotation.
[05:18] Katrina: Speaking of keys, we need to understand Redwood's key rotation cadence for CMEK when you manage the key vs the customer-manages scenario.
[05:26] Maya: If the customer manages the KMS, you control rotation. If Redwood manages the KMS (hosted), we rotate keys on a 90-day schedule for root-level props and maintain rotation logs; we can provide KMS audit records. For compliance we can also support HSM-backed keys if required.
[05:44] [00:06:00] Liam: For the EMEA pilot we likely need customer-managed keys in-region. Is there a hard blocker to spinning up a private VPC in eu-west-1?
[06:00] Jae: No hard blocker — we've spun private VPCs in-region before. It requires a two-week lead time for networking and KMS provisioning and we do a security onboarding checklist.
[06:12] Priya: Two weeks is fine but we have a freeze window 12/24-1/2, so realistically we want provisioning completed before the freeze.
[06:22] Maya: We'll aim to accelerate the setup. I'll add an action item to confirm provisioning lead times.
[06:30] [00:07:00] Katrina: On audit logs, the report called out missing authentication headers in logs, implying our SIEM didn't get some events. Is there a reliable webhook or delivery guarantee for log forwarding?
[06:42] Jae: Logs can be pushed via secure syslog, S3 export, or direct SIEM connectors; we provide retries with backoff. For Private you can host a collector in the VPC for near-real time ingestion.
[06:56] Tom: Do you provide signed logs or WORM storage for immutability?
[07:02] Maya: We can enable signed log export to S3 with Object Lock for WORM semantics in Private; hosted can be configured similarly if you bring your own AWS account for exports.
[07:16] [00:08:00] Katrina: The other issue — SAML assertion skew under load — what metrics or tracing can we use to debug?
[07:26] Jae: We emit auth latency histograms and assertion timestamp offsets in the trace events; we can share a sample query for your tracing backend. That should let you correlate spikes with load.
[07:38] Priya: For the CVE remediation — what's Redwood's policy for patching third-party libs in the runtime? Is there a weekly cadence or do you triage by severity?
[07:48] Maya: We triage by severity: critical/active exploit gets an expedited patch (24–72h for hosted images), high/medium are scheduled into our weekly build train with canary deploys. We'll share the SLA doc for that.
[08:02] [00:09:00] Liam: For our internal process we want a reproducible plan: if a critical CVE is found, we want a patched image, a canary rollout in staging, an automated regression smoke, and a rollback plan — can Redwood deliver the patched image and a runbook?
[08:18] Jae: Yes, we'll supply the patched image, a runbook for canarying and rollback points, and a checklist for smoke tests. We can also run the canary ourselves if you want Redwood SE to coordinate.
[08:30] Katrina: That would help. Also auditors asked about documented SDLC gates — do you have a template we can adopt for merge blockers and emergency exceptions?
[08:40] Maya: We have a secure SDLC playbook and a merge-gate template we use with customers; I'll attach that. It's not prescriptive but it covers SCA, pre-merge E2E test, and a CR process for emergency patches.
[08:54] [00:09:50] Priya: A nit: the report shows some unencrypted backups in staging — is that a Redwood snapshotting policy or our overlay?
[09:02] Jae: By default Redwood snapshots are encrypted at rest; if an overlay or external backup pipeline copied data out unencrypted that'd be on the customer side. We can help inspect the snapshot inventory.
[09:14] Tom: Ok, please run an inventory check with us.
[09:18] Maya: noted.
[09:22] [00:10:30] Katrina: For the triage rubric — we'd like to align severity mapping (what Sentinel calls P0/P1) to Redwood's CVSS mapping, so we have consistent SLA expectations.
[09:36] Maya: Good point — we'll draft a mapping table (CVSS -> Sentinel priority) and circulate.
[09:42] Jae: Also, small note on remediation testing: some fixes require model recompilation that can affect latency; we'll flag regression risks and provide quantized test results.
[09:56] Liam: That's important — we can't regress 95th percentile latency by more than 10% for the pilot.
[10:02] [00:11:20] Priya: Are there any live exploits out in the wild for the RCE? The report wasn't clear.
[10:10] Katrina: Vendor said there's a PoC but no wide exploitation yet. It still counts as urgent.
[10:16] Jae: We'll treat as high. We'll also add a smoke test harness to test the exploit vector in staging — safe repro with logs.
[10:26] [00:12:00] Maya: Quick recap of agreed items so far: Redwood to send SOC 2 evidence + security packet; Jae to prepare patched image and staging runbook; Sentinel to share prioritized CVE list and triage rubric. Anything missing?
[12:40] Katrina: Can we get the mitigation ETA for the RCE by Friday?
[12:46] Jae: I'll aim for an initial ETA by Friday 2025-12-19 assuming no regressions show up in our test suite.
[12:52] Tom: Also we need a note on data residency and whether audit logs can remain in eu-west-1 only.
[13:00] Maya: We'll confirm that in the security packet.
[13:06] [00:13:30] Priya: One last technical ask: for Private, what's the recommended key rotation cadence for session keys vs data encryption keys?
[13:18] Jae: Session keys are short TTLs — typically rotated hourly for tokens. Data encryption (CMEK) rotation is customer-controlled; if customer rotates keys frequently we recommend automated key rollover with re-encryption windows during off-peak. We'll add recommended cadence (monthly for CMEK rotation is common in some customers, but depends on compliance).
[13:40] [00:14:20] Liam: On auditability — can you attach a chain-of-custody for logs when exporting to our S3? We'll need signatures for each export batch.
[14:00] Maya: Yes, signed manifests + checksum metadata are standard with our export tool.
[14:06] [00:15:00] Katrina: Great. Anything else? If not let's do roll call for next steps.
[15:00] Maya: Ok next steps recap — we'll share: security packet w/ SOC2, canary/patch runbook, CI SCA snippets, image SBOMs. You'll share the prioritized CVE list and triage rubric. We'll schedule the exploit repro session in early Jan.
[15:24] Priya: Sounds good.
[15:28] Tom: Thanks all.
[15:30] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.

Closing notes (auto):
